title: Call digest, version 1
description:
One call's identity, coverage, usage, metric aggregates, finding counts and references to paginated detail.

This is a saved fact, not a view: everything in it was computed by the processor from archived sources, and a reader does no counter arithmetic to render it. The detail refs are the only way into per-participant, per-stream, per-path, timeline and finding data, and each is read against this digest's `revision` — a reader that pins one revision and pages another has spliced two generations together.

schemaVersion.description: Major version. A reader that does not support this exact value must refuse the document rather than read it field by field — a field whose meaning changed would otherwise render as if it had not.

roomId.description: Null when the sources never carried one. A room id may be a UUID with no relationship to the call id, so nothing may be inferred from its text.

revision.description: This immutable output generation. Detail pages are valid only against it.

lifecycle.description: An open call is provisional even when every currently known file was processed: more samples may still arrive. `unknown` means no lifecycle evidence of sufficient authority was found.

range.description: The known call span — not the archive write time, and not a summary's finalization time. Null when lifecycle evidence cannot establish it. First and last observed samples may bound observed exposure but do not establish authoritative join or leave times.

capabilities.description: Must contain every key the contract requires (see registry/capabilities.v1.json, which both implementations and the conformance suite read). Additional keys are allowed.

sources.description: The immutable input inventory this generation was built from. Its hash plus policy identity is `provenance.sourceRevision`, which is what makes a retry deterministic and a late arrival detectable.

participantSessions.description: Deduplicated client lifecycle instances. Never unique people, and never a sum of per-SFU counts — the same client seen by two SFUs is one session.

peakConcurrentParticipants.description: Requires membership intervals. A summary's single-call peak may be used when authoritative for the whole call; peaks from several SFUs may not be summed, because two SFUs peaking at different moments never co-occurred.

observedParticipantMs.description: The union of valid observation intervals per client instance, summed across instances. Not participant count multiplied by call duration.

connectedParticipantMs.description: Requires explicit connection-state evidence. Null when there is none — not a fallback to observed time.
